newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade thin at $62 -feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade thin at $62 -feedlots.

text.p: Feedlot cattle near midday Tuesday in Kansas and the Texas Panhandle area sold at $62.00 per cwt in light volume, unchanged from Monday's brisk sales, feedlot sources said. The price was down $1.00 from last week, feedlot sources said.
About 500 steers and heifers likely to grade select and choice sold in Kansas following nearly 43,000 traded on Monday. Week-to-date trade totaled about 49,500 head.
An estimated 1,000 head sold in the Texas Panhandle/ western Oklahoma area, bringing the week-to-date figure near 83,000 after Monday's sales of about 56,500, sources said.
Fed cattle prices this week were pressured by a seasonal drop in beef demand and a large supply of market-ready cattle, particularly in the Texas Panhandle, feedlot sources said.

Outlooks for continued large numbers of market-ready cattle through the month provided plenty of incentive for feedlots to stay current even if it meant selling cattle at a loss, several sources said. At $62.00, owners lost about $50.00 per head on average, several sources said.
Losses were not seen lasting more than three to four weeks, with cattle supplies seen dropping into the fall starting in August, which could bring prices back into profitable territory, they said.
